named_competitor_comparison.AgentAntibody: PARTIAL — runtime adaptive memory/responses for user boundary; not discrete L0–L3 SUC intensity controller vs fixed levels.
named_competitor_comparison.AutoDojo: BACKGROUND/COMPLEMENTARY — adaptive black-box attack optimizer; not a defense; stresses AG evolving-eval gap.
named_competitor_comparison.COPA: PARTIAL — continual training-time preference optimization on evolving attacks; different operating regime from AG runtime levels.
named_competitor_comparison.SecOPD: BACKGROUND/ADJACENT — token-level training distillation vs adaptive PI; static after train.
named_competitor_comparison.Adaptive Adversaries: BACKGROUND/COMPLEMENTARY — multi-turn adaptive attacker benchmark; not a defense.
named_competitor_comparison.SCOUT: PARTIAL — closest on safety–utility–cost (latency) adaptive allocation; allocates detectors, not intervention levels.
named_competitor_comparison.Task Shield: PARTIAL — test-time task alignment verification with strong AgentDojo SUC; fixed checker, no level policy adaptation.
named_competitor_comparison.PIGuard: PARTIAL — over-defense-aware PI detector; no runtime escalate/de-escalate intervention levels.
named_competitor_comparison.VIGIL: PARTIAL — verify-before-commit tool-stream defense with security–utility balance; no discrete adaptive levels.
named_competitor_comparison.SafeHarness: PARTIAL (highest mechanism overlap) — discrete privilege degradation 0–4 with escalate + safe-window de-escalate; different level semantics/triggers/objectives than AG.

final_research_gap: No audited paper fully combines: (i) discrete runtime intervention levels with sanitize/restrict/block semantics, (ii) attack-triggered escalation plus legitimate-task defense-cost-triggered de-escalation, (iii) mixed attack/legitimate workload comparison against fixed levels under unified ASR/utility/defense-cost, and (iv) AutoDojo-class adaptive black-box attacker evaluation. SafeHarness covers (partial) discrete escalate/de-escalate levels; SCOUT covers detector-side SUC-latency allocation; COPA/HARD/AutoDojo cover evolving/adaptive regimes AG does not yet match. The remaining defensible gap is methodological/protocol: mixed-workload SUC study of AG’s intervention-level controller vs fixed and escalate-only policies — contingent on dropping uniqueness claims for discrete adaptive levels.

verdict_detail: A narrow methodological novelty remains for the mixed-workload fixed-vs-adaptive discrete intervention-level SUC protocol (C2). Algorithmic uniqueness of escalate/de-escalate discrete levels is blocked by SafeHarness (C1 PARTIALLY NOVEL). Historical contribution is unsupported (C3). Evolving-attacker robustness is not a novel AG claim under current evidence (C4 EXISTING elsewhere / LIMITED for AG). Overall: NOVELTY REQUIRES REFINEMENT via claim rewrite; no mandatory core redesign.
